role: The full CI workflow ("CI"): manual-only (workflow_dispatch with scope gates|unit|full and optional baseline-ref) and reusable (workflow_call, scope default full) so testflight.yml gates releases on it. Four jobs: lint-and-budgets (macOS, every static gate), strict-concurrency (ubuntu), thread-sanitizer and tests (macOS, skipped for gates scope).
toplevel: Triggers: workflow_dispatch only (no push/PR/schedule) and workflow_call. Top-level permissions contents:read; concurrency cancels an in-flight run on the same workflow+ref (when called from testflight.yml, github.workflow is the caller's name). Scope gates runs lint-and-budgets + strict-concurrency only; unit adds TSan and the unit test target (coverage not gated); full adds the UI target and the coverage floors. scripts/simulate_ci.sh (make ci-local) parses this file to replay it locally, and scripts/check_gates_wired.sh requires every check_/enforce_ script name to appear in it. Since nothing triggers it automatically, every gate that exists only here runs only when someone dispatches it or deploys to TestFlight.

flags.text: "Every gate is wired into CI" (check_gates_wired.sh) only checks that each scripts/check_*/enforce_* name appears as text in ci.yml, a workflow that never runs on push (workflow_dispatch/workflow_call only). A gate present in ci.yml but missing from the push-triggered gates.yml passes this check yet never runs automatically (see coremotion/hr-feed guards).

units.does: Computes the budget baseline: inputs.baseline-ref if given, else HEAD~1 if it exists, else HEAD if .ci has uncommitted changes, else emits empty value/require and exits 0. Verifies the ref resolves to a commit (else exit 1), then writes value=<sha> and require=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.

branches.effect: choose a default (next branches); otherwise use the given ref

branches.cond: root commit and `git diff --quiet HEAD -- .ci` reports changes
branches.effect: baseline = HEAD (working tree compared); else outputs value= and require= empty, prints root-commit message and exits 0 so the next step skips without failing

branches.cond: chosen ref does not resolve to a commit
branches.effect: print refusal and exit 1 (job fails); else output value and require=1

flags.text: The budget ratchet compares only against the parent commit (HEAD~1). gates.yml runs once per push, so in a push of several commits a budget raised in any commit but the last is never compared; ci.yml is manual-only, so raises in commits between manual runs are never compared either. The `budget-raise-ok` trailer scan (git log BASE..HEAD) has the same one-commit window.

units.does: Runs scripts/check_budget_monotonicity.sh with BUDGET_BASE_REF/BUDGET_REQUIRE_BASELINE from the baseline step: fails on a raised ceiling or lowered min_* floor not acknowledged by a budget-raise-ok trailer; with require=1 an unresolvable baseline fails instead of skipping.

flags.text: .ci/min_coverage_views.txt holds 43.5, a non-integer; check_budget_monotonicity.sh read_int() rejects anything not ^[0-9]+$ and the loop `continue`s, so the views coverage floor is never compared and can be lowered with no budget-raise-ok trailer while the ratchet prints clean. Its header lists only three floors (min_coverage, min_coverage_logic, min_localization_coverage).

flags.text: ci.yml's tests-job comment says that on `unit` scope run_tests_with_coverage.sh 'reports coverage without gating it', and run_tests_with_coverage.sh's own header says unit scope 'gates on the LOGIC floor alone'. Neither is true: unit scope exports SKIP_OVERALL_COVERAGE and SKIP_LOGIC_COVERAGE, but check_coverage.sh enforces the Views floor (.ci/min_coverage_views.txt, 43.5) on every run, so a unit-scope dispatch can fail on views coverage.
